# Preface

This site is the support for the **"Advanced Programming and Parallel Computing"** module of
the MIASHS master's degree (Mathematics and Computer Science Applied to the Humanities and
Social Sciences), Université Paul-Valéry Montpellier 3.

The module covers six families of techniques: asynchronous programming, inter-process
communication and locks, distributed computing (Dask, Ray), SIMD, GPU and WebGPU.

This module rests on a *self-directed, co-constructed* learning design: two tracks are
offered, one with an AI tutor that you design and improve yourself, the other with classic
learning from the resources. The technical objectives are identical; only the learning
process differs. You will find all the details on the [Teaching design](teaching-design.qmd)
page.

You can browse the site like a book: use the table of contents on the left. Before the first
session, follow the [Prerequisites](prerequisites.qmd) page to install your tooling.

The [Session 1 slides](slides/2026-08-26-seance-1-slides.html) are available as a standalone
deck (same content as the first two chapters). New to large language models? Start with this
[short general introduction to LLMs](https://chatgpt-imag-talk-francoisdavid-collin-f46d6064936d62b9b50d038c.pages.math.cnrs.fr/).
